paper.title: Catalytic effect of water on calcium carbonate decomposition

primary_full_source_actually_read.author: Guido Giammaria
primary_full_source_actually_read.title: CaCO3 decomposition enhanced by dielectric barrier discharge plasma. The effect of plasma-catalysis.
primary_full_source_actually_read.scope: Thermal experiments without plasma, Chapter 2 and Appendix A2
primary_full_source_actually_read.license: All rights reserved; full PDF/pages and complete source code are not redistributed

specimen.preparation: 20% O2/N2, atmospheric, 900 C 30 min; pelletize at 160 bar, crush and sieve 250-300 um
specimen.conditioning: 40 absorption/decomposition cycles; kinetic experiments cycles 41-131, with source aging corrections
specimen.aging_correction: Standard 630 C dry experiment every 5-10 cycles; source reports 5% decay in cycles 40-60, five-week air storage then recovery, subsequent 25% decrease over 70 cycles
specimen.plateau_scope: Initial decomposition before about 50% carbonate exhaustion. Source rejects plateaus below 1 min, flags 1-2 min for possible rate underestimation.
specimen.co2_boundary: No feed CO2 during decomposition; Ar with 0-1.25% H2O; outlet CO2 measured by calibrated MS and below equilibrium per authors
specimen.water_arrival: Tubing adsorption delayed steam arrival by about 30 s in one experiment; fitted plateaus are not gas-switch transient data
specimen.uncertainty: Rate margins from experimental reproducibility; water pressure margins from <5 ppm Ar contamination and flow mixing; no joint covariance supplied

rate_definition.locator: printed pages 44-50, Eq 2.1, Table 2.1; Appendix A2 printed pages 168-170
rate_definition.normalization_interpretation: The table k times site density gives total specimen mol/s. Table k cannot be interpreted as s^-1 or reused as an intrinsic per-area turnover constant; active specimen area is absorbed in the fitted values.
rate_definition.appendix_parameterization: Appendix instead directly fits total mol/s limiting rates, fixing dry rate to its first observed rate; pressure at that first row is 2.5e-6 bar, not exactly zero.
rate_definition.surface_intermediate: Assumed Langmuir equilibrium; proposed bicarbonate and OH pathways not uniquely distinguished by kinetics. No independent surface-intermediate free energies or transient inventories supplied.
rate_definition.thermodynamic_feedback: No reverse rate or CO2 inhibition term; cannot extrapolate to equilibrium, carbonation, or whole-brick transport.
